claims: C1 the root level is the highest level of instruction authority
C2 a root rule cannot be overridden by a system message
C3 a root rule cannot be overridden by a developer
C4 a root rule cannot be overridden by a user

concepts.name: root_rule
concepts.gloss: R is a fundamental root rule of the instruction hierarchy

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: which of two instruction authority levels is the higher one, per the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority

concepts.name: root_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the root level of the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: system_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the system level of the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: developer_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer level of the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: user_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user level of the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause says root rules cannot be overridden by system messages, developers or users, so each instruction must carry the level it was issued at for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: overrides
concepts.gloss: instruction I would override instruction J if both were followed
concepts.inference: 'cannot be overridden' relates a root rule to a conflicting instruction from a lower level; which pairs conflict is a fact about the case

ontology.gloss: I is a root rule, hence an instruction at the root level
I is an instruction issued at the system level
I is an instruction issued at the developer level
I is an instruction issued at the user level
